events.text: The village teacher's cane has a name: Wisdom. It visits your palm for the third time this week.

effects.log: The characters stick. So does the sting.
By winter the cane bounces off. The teacher looks at your hand with new respect.

events.text: Recitation day: every child stands and recites the Thousand Character Classic from memory. You are next.

ok.log: Every character, no stumbles. The teacher nods once, which is like a parade.

fail.log: You forget the second half and invent a new one. The class laughs; the teacher does not.

effects.log: The whole class learns it your way. The teacher gives up.

events.text: The biggest boy in school claims your desk by the window.

ok.log: The window seat is yours. So is the respect of the smaller children.

fail.log: You end up under the desk. For now.

effects.log: You sit by the door and eat very well.

events.text: The school holds a poetry contest. The prize is a real brush with a wolf-hair tip.

ok.log: Your poem wins. The brush is the first thing you ever truly own.

fail.log: Your poem about the mountains is mostly about lunch.

effects.log: It does not win. Your mother keeps it for the rest of her life.

events.text: Arithmetic with the abacus: clack, clack, clack. The fastest child gets to leave early.

ok.log: You leave early every day for a month.

fail.log: You finish last and count beads in your sleep.

effects.log: You leave last, but three children can finally count.

events.text: The river is warm, the fish are jumping, and school is very, very boring today.

effects.log: The best day of the summer. The cane the next morning is very efficient.
The teacher tells a story about a swordsman. The fish will be there tomorrow.

events.text: The monks teach reading from the sutras, which are long, and arithmetic from the rice accounts, which are short.

effects.log: The words are strange, but your breath slows when you chant them.
You find an error in the temple books. The abbot is very quiet, then very pleased.

events.text: At dawn the young monks practise forms in the courtyard. The abbot pretends not to see you copying from behind a pillar.

effects.log: Your stance improves. The abbot moves the pillar a little closer, somehow.
'Sweep first,' says the abbot. You sweep for a year. Then you join.

events.text: Your tutor is a failed official who takes out his disappointments on the Analects, and on you.

effects.log: You win a grudging nod. From him, it is a festival.
He screams. You are punished. It was worth it.

events.text: Your tutor, it turns out, was once a swordsman. You catch him practising alone at dawn.

effects.log: He sighs, and adds swordsmanship to your lessons. Nobody at home ever finds out.
He notices. Your lessons become slightly easier.

events.text: A classmate has no lunch again. You notice she always has no lunch.

effects.log: You are hungrier and happier. She never forgets it.
The teacher quietly arranges rice for her. Nobody else ever knows.

events.text: The end-of-year examination. Your teacher paces between the desks like a general.

ok.log: First in the class. Your name goes on the wall.

fail.log: Somewhere in the middle, like most of the world.

effects.log: You are both caught. You both copy the Analects ten times.

events.text: After school, the children tell ghost stories in the empty schoolroom until someone screams.

effects.log: Three children do not sleep for a week. You are a legend.
You never live it down. You also never forget how much fun it was.

events.text: The last day of school. The teacher gives each child one sentence of advice to carry out into the world.

effects.log: 'Read people, not just books.' You remember it all your life.
'Greedy,' he says, and smiles. 'Be kind when it costs you something.'

events.text: You discover the school's single battered copy of 'The Tale of the Nine Heroes' and read it under the desk.

effects.log: You dream of swords for a month. Your grades suffer. Your heart does not.
Soon the whole class is a sect of nine heroes with bamboo swords.

events.text: The magistrate visits the school and asks each child to write one character. He will choose the best to hang in his hall.

ok.log: Yours is chosen. It hangs in the magistrate's hall for twenty years.

fail.log: Your "courage" looks nervous. The magistrate is kind about it.

effects.log: The magistrate laughs and gives you a sweet.

events.text: A new student arrives from the city, in silk, with a servant carrying his books. The class hates him at once.

effects.log: He is lonely and funny. You become friends for life.
He cries in the courtyard. You feel worse than he does.

events.text: The teacher falls ill, and the school is closed. The children run wild for a month.

effects.log: He is so surprised he recovers a week early. The class is not pleased with you.
The best month of your childhood. You climb every tree in the county.
